## 5.95 Operation: 08.05 Output Option - Value Search with profile

You can specify a profile instead of specifying a set of weighted criteria. A profile is a predefined set of weighted criteria in a specific currency, for example, 20€ per connection and 30€ to arrive between 7 PM and 10 PM.  
  
As markets have different specificities and travel habits, Amadeus has predefined profiles per market with their associated criteria and weights.  
  
The profile name has the following pattern:

Generic profile prefix  

1A

Market (country code)

Argentina (AR), Australia (AU), Belgium (BE), Brazil (BR), China (CN), Colombia (CE), Denmark (DK), Finland (FI), France (FR), Germany (DE), India (IN), Italy (IT), Japan (JP), Mexico (MX), Netherlands (NL), New Zealand (NZ), Norway (NO), Russia (RU), South Africa (ZA), Spain (ES), Sweden (CH), Ukraine (UA), United Kingdom (GB), United States (US)

Week/short stay/long stay

Business (BU)  
Weekend Gateway (WG)  
Others (OT)

International/Domestic

International (INT)  
Domestic (DOM)  
Exception for Belgium and Netherlands  
Continental (CON)  
Intercontinental (ITC)

Popularity

POP

  
  
 

  
For example, the profile name 1A\_GB\_BU\_INT\_POP corresponds to GB market, business, international, popularity.  
  
The example below illustrates a query with value search profile specified.  
  

## 5.95.1 Query Structure

![](/resources/externalFiles/images/userguideeditor/icon_collapse.gif)XML Example

<Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoardSearch xmlns="http://xml.amadeus.com/FMPTBQ\_24\_6\_1A"> <numberOfUnit> <unitNumberDetail> <numberOfUnits>1</numberOfUnits> <typeOfUnit>PX</typeOfUnit> </unitNumberDetail> </numberOfUnit> <paxReference> <ptc>ADT</ptc> <traveller> <ref>1</ref> </traveller> </paxReference> <valueSearch> <criteriaName>1A\_GB\_BU\_INT\_POP</criteriaName> </valueSearch> <itinerary> <requestedSegmentRef> <segRef>1</segRef> </requestedSegmentRef> <departureLocalization> <departurePoint> <locationId>LON</locationId> </departurePoint> </departureLocalization> <arrivalLocalization> <arrivalPointDetails> <locationId>PAR</locationId> </arrivalPointDetails> </arrivalLocalization> <timeDetails> <firstDateTimeDetail> <date>101216</date> </firstDateTimeDetail> </timeDetails> </itinerary> <itinerary> <requestedSegmentRef> <segRef>2</segRef> </requestedSegmentRef> <departureLocalization> <departurePoint> <locationId>PAR</locationId> </departurePoint> </departureLocalization> <arrivalLocalization> <arrivalPointDetails> <locationId>LON</locationId> </arrivalPointDetails> </arrivalLocalization> <timeDetails> <firstDateTimeDetail> <date>171216</date> </firstDateTimeDetail> </timeDetails> </itinerary> </Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoardSearch>

## 5.97 Operation: 08.07 Output Option - Fare Family information

Depending on Office ID setting and input option (FFI), Master Pricer can return:

-   The airline fare family name at fare component level and/or at requested segment level.
-   The airline fare family tier/rank (explicit activation required).
-   The airline fare family description per requested segment consistently with airline filling:
    -   The services included in the fare family for free
    -   The services that can be bought at a charge
    -   The services that are not valid for this fare family but that should be displayed to the customer.

Input option: FFI with 3 values (1, 2 or 3)

Fare family information value

1

2

3

FF name at fare component level

x

x

x

FF tier/rank

x

x

x

Resulting FF name at requested segment level

x

x

Services of the resulting FF

x

**Syntax output example** :

  <familyInformation>  
      <refNumber>1</refNumber>  
      <fareFamilyname>VALUE</fareFamilyname>  
      <hierarchy>5</hierarchy>      #tier/rank  
      <description>ECONOMY VALUE</description>  
      <carrier>6X</carrier>  
      <services>  
          <reference>1</reference>  
          <status>INC</status>  
      </services>  
      <...>  
  </familyInformation>

For each service, the output should include commercial description (text) filed in by the airline as well as the OC subcode.

In the following example,

At fare component level:

-   Fare family VALUE is applied on fare component LON-NYC.
-   Fare family BASIC is applied on fare component NYC-LON.

At requested segment level:

-   Fare family VALUE is applied on the outbound.
-   Fare family BASIC is applied on the inbound.

VALUE fare family description:

-   Fare Family short description: ECONOMY VALUE
-   Services included:
    -   OC Sub code: LMS
    -   Commercial description: LIGHT MEAL SNACK
-   Services at a charge:
    -   OC Sub code CB5
    -   Commercial description: CHNG BEF DEP 50 EUR

BASIC Fare family description:

-   Fare family short description: ECONOMY BASIC
-   Services included:
    -   OC Sub code: LMS
    -   Commercial description: LIGHT MEAL SNACK
-   Services not offered:
    -   OC Sub code CB0
    -   Commercial description: CHNG BEF DEP

**Note for NDC users**

Fare Family short name (also called brand code) is available for NDC content only from Master Pricer Travel Board 21.4.

Fare Family name (also called short description - in the "description" field) is available for NDC content as long as Fare Families are available.

## 5.98 Operation: 08.08 Output Option - Return flight duration at segment level

The flight duration can be returned at segment level. This option is triggered by a Fare Search parameter.

In this example:

IAD-SFO UA 492: the flight duration is 06H00

SFO-DFW AA 1052: the flight duration is 03H15

DFW-IAD AA 1489: The flight duration is 02H50

## 5.99 Operation: 08.09 Output Option - Commission returned

The user has the ability to have the commission (in percentage) for each fare basis returnd in output of Master Pricer. This is triggered by Office ID setting  
When the commission is filed directly in percentage, the filed value is returned.  
When the commission is filed in amount, the percentage returned is calculated on the filed selling amount.  
  
  
The example below illustrates recommendations with commission percentage (13.34 %) returned for each fare component.

## 5.101 Operation: 08.11 Output option - Return Airline Alliance

The user has the ability to have the Airline Alliance code at flight level in the reply.

The functionality is triggered by a setting at OID level.

In the example, 2 Alliances are returned:

-   LAN: oneworld (\*O)
-   Lufthansa: StarAlliance (\*A)

## 5.102 Operation: 08.12 Output Option : Itinerary Upsell

The Upsell option returns up to 6 (this can be limited due to operational impact) alternative recommendations attached to higher fare family than the basic recommendation one.  
The price of the upsell recommendation is higher than the basic recommendation price.  
  
The itinerary upsell option applies at itinerary level based on the resulting fare family for the whole itinerary

  
In case of itinerary upsell request, eligible recommendations that will propose an upsell involves mandatory the same marketing carrier cross all bounds and segments  
  
The order of upsell is driven by increasing price of the recommendations and not the tier of the upsell fare family.  
  
A recommendation containing an upsell is called "eligible". If an upsell recommendation has itself an upsell , this upsell is moved to the eligible one.

## 5.103 Operation: 08.13 Output Option : Homogeneous Upsell

The Upsell option returns up to 6 (this can be limited due to operational impact) alternative recommendations attached to higher fare family than the basic recommendation one .

The price of the upsell recommendation is higher than the basic recommendation price.

The Homogeneous Upsell allows you to return all the recommendations having the same fare family at fare component level for a given itinerary. The option is an additional feature of the Itinerary Upsell UPH returning up to 6 upsells. It is triggered by the ‘’UFH’’ code in the feeType field.

<feeIdDescription>

            <feeId\>

                        <feeType\>UFH</feeType\>

                        <feeIdNumber>1</feeIdNumber>

            </feeId>

</feeIdDescription>

The UFH code must always be followed by the number 1 in the <feeIdNumber\> otherwise an error message is returned. Please see the error message description below.

The number of Upsell recommendations requested is given by the UPH feeIdNumber (up to 6 recommendations).

## 5.104 Operation: 08.14 Output Option : More Upsells

### Description

More Upsells option is an upgrade of Upsell option allowing to exceed the maximum number of upsell recommendations returned to the end user.

### Activation

The activation of this option is made by input (MUP) additional to the classic Upsell option and a specific configuration is needed to allow the use of More Upsells.

## 5.105 Operation: 08.15 Output option - Airline Fare Family with MySearch family

When using MY SEARCH for the definition of Parameterized Fare Families in the query of Master Pricer, and depending on Office ID authorization, it is possible to display, alongside the parameterized fare families information,  the matching airline fare family information (FFI), in Master Pricer Output.

Compatibility of MY SEARCH and FFI is possible for the following FFI values in input :

Fare family information value

1

2

3

FF name at fare component level

x

x

x

FF tier/rank

x

x

x

Resulting FF name at requested segment level

x

x

Services of the resulting FF

x

Syntax output example :

Under the "FAF" segment, Parameterized Fare Families are displayed as they were defined by the user in the input query

\[…\]

FAF+1+BUSINESS+40'

FAF+2+ECONOMY+20'

\[…\]

Also, Airline Fare Families are displayed under the FAF segment.

\[…\]

FAF+3+ECONLIGHT++++ECONOMY LIGHT+CX+1:INC2:INC3:CHA4:CHA5:INC6:CHA'

FAF+4+NBASICE++++BASIC ECO+SV+7:CHA8:CHA9:CHA10:CHA11:CHA12:INC13:INC'

\[…\]

Airline Fare Families and Parameterized Fare Families have unique indexes under the FAF segment. And it is possible to differentiate the two based on the fact that Airline Fare Families have the Airline code displayed in the "FAF" segment, as opposed to the Parameterized Fare Family.

Both the airline fare family and the parameterized fare family are referenced at both Itinerary level and fare component level.

Parameterized Fare Families are referenced using the code-set "F", whereas the airline fare families are referenced using the code-set "AFF".

For the case of a One-Way travel

On recommendation level, the user can see a reference to the Airline Fare Family index through AFF

\[…\]

ITM+5'

REF+F:2\*AFF:3'

\[…\]

Also, the Airline Fare Family is referenced under each fare component

\[…\]

ODR+1'

FDI+W::M:9+WETFLXE0:ADT:RP++N'

REF+F:2\*AFF:3'

FDI+W::M:9+WETFLXE0:ADT:RP++Y'

FCC+FCA+162.62'

REF+F:2\*AFF:3'

PDI++M'

\[…\]

In case of a round-trip or open-jaw, having two ODR segments for each segment, the resulting fare family (fare family having the highest rank)  is shown at recommendation level:

-   For the Parameterized Fare Family, the resulting fare family for the whole itinerary
-   For the Airline Fare Family, the resulting fare family for each bound

ITM+5'

REF+F:2\*AFF:3\*:6'

\[…\]

ODR+1'

FDI+W::M:9+WETFLXE0:ADT:RP++N'

REF+F:2\*AFF:3'

FDI+W::M:9+WETFLXE0:ADT:RP++Y'

FCC+FCA+162.62'

REF+F:2\*AFF:3'

PDI++M'

ODR+2'

FDI+S::M:9+SETCLSE0:ADT:RP++N'

REF+F:1\*AFF:6'

FDI+S::M:9+SETCLSE0:ADT:RP++Y'

FCC+FCA+113.96'

REF+F:1\*AFF:6'

PDI++M'

## 5.107 Operation: 09.02 Output Option - Fare Calculation

This option allows the user to request the entire fare calculation.  
  
When the FS Parameter  Gb\_Fare\_Calculation is set, the following information is displayed:

-   Fare Details Information: 
    -   The Total amount per fare component (FCA)
    -   The Q surcharges per segment of a fare component (Q)
    -   The Stopover surcharges per segment of a fare component (S)
    -   The Mileage per fare component (M)

-   Conversion rate information:
    -   The fare calculation currency
    -   The rate of exchange
-   Passenger information:
    
    -   The taxes details.

## 5.110 Operation: 09.05 Output Option - Area Exclusion from Recommendations

In the input of this webservice, it is possible to specify the exclusion in output of all recommendations with an Origin from a given list of prohibited countries.  
  
The list must be set in the input under the <flighInformation> section in <exclusionDetailArea>.  
The option "N" in <areaQualifier> allows you to specify that the list of <areaId> are countries.  
  
**Example :**  
To exclude all recommendations from three countries : France (FR), Germany (DE), United Kingdom (GB). The information must be mapped in the <flightInfo\> section as followed :  
  
<flightInfo\>  
            <exclusionDetailArea>  
                <identifierExclusion>X</identifierExclusion>  
                <areaQualifier>N</areaQualifier>  
<areaId>FR</areaId>  
<areaId>DE</areaId>  
<areaId>GB</areaId>  
            </exclusionDetailArea>  
        </flightInfo\>

## 5.111 Operation: 09.06 Output Option - Exclude Cities, Airports and date from Recommendations

In order to maximize the quantity of Non-StopRecommendations and eliminate duplicated recommendations with the restof split queries, the service allows the possibility to exclude a range of city, airport, dates and journeys. Three options apply.

  
1\. Non-Stop Excluded Recommendations to exclude all non stp recommendations in response.Journeys containing only non-stop flights are excluded. In case of more than one requested segment, journeys contain at least one proposed segment with direct/connecting flight.

The input option has to include the XNS code set in the TFI segment as shown in the example below. 

  
2\. Flexible Dates: Central Date Excluded Recommendations to exclude all central dates and recommendations in response

  
The input option has to include the XDR code set in the TFI segment as shown in the example below. 

  
3\. Radius Option: Main City / Airport Code Excluded Recommendations to exclude location such as airport and city. 

The input option has to include the XRC code set in the TFI segment as shown in the example below.

## 5.112 Operation: 09.07 Output Option - Amenity

The Master Pricer Travel Board search gives you the possibility to retrieve Route Happy Rich Content. The Amenity content evaluates the specific details (fares, products and services) of an airline offer.

The Amenity content is given in output of Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoard search at a granularity associating this content for each Cabin Class of the proposed travel solutions for a given itinerary.

### How to Read the Amenity Details

In the service grammar, the details of the Amenity is given in the <amenities> section of the <amenitiesGroup>. More specifically, the amenities information is given by the repetitions of the <amenityDetails> section contained in <amenities>. Each repetition gives information on **one** specific amenity (e.g. POWER amenity giving the information that USB IS AVAILABLE on board with Fees). 

**Example :** 

In the following example, two amenities are returned. This is shown by the repetition of the <amenityDetails> section.

<amenitiesGroup>

<amentities>

<amenityDetails>

<amenityReference>1</amenityReference>

<amenityType>P</amenityType>

</amenityDetails>

<amenityDetails>

<amenityReference>2</amenityReference>

<amenityType>B</amenityType>

</amenityDetails>

</amentities>

</amenitiesGroup>

**Important Note:** Each amenity is returned with a given "reference" number (<amenityReference>). This number allows to relate the amenity details to the specific Cabin Class of the flight given in the proposed travel solutions which offers such service. It is important to specify that several flights/Cabin Class may share the same Amenity. If this is the case, the same Amenity reference number is used inside the different Travel Solution structures. More details about the relation between the Amenity and the associated Cabin Class of the flights is described in the following section.

Inside the Amenity group, several fields are used. Each one displays a specific information on the Amenity. The table below provides additional information about the fields usage.

Field

Usage Description

<amenityReference>

ID of the Amenity, used in the <referencingDetail\> group associated to the cabin class.

<amenityType>

Defines the Type of the amenity (e.g. POWER, ENTERTAINEMENT, BEVERAGE etc)

<amenityAttribute>

Each type is composed of several Attribute (e.g. POWER type can have both "USB outlet" "Outlet" etc).

<isChargeable>

This is a boolean. Used to indicate whether the amenity is free of charge (code set 0 used) or chargeable (code set 1 used)

<seatSpace\>

Used when the amenity Type is referencing the the SEAT. Gives the number of inches of a seat pitch (distance from any point on one seat to the same point on the front seat).

<seatSpaceUnit>

Associated to the SeatSpace value, gives the information on the unit used (cm, inches). If nothing displayed, the information is referencing to inches.

<seatflateness>

Provides information on the orientation of the seat.

<rowLayout>

Provides information on the Cabin layout. This field is an integer where each number gives the number of seat per row (e.g. 242 => 3 columns of 2seats-4seats-2seats).

**Note** : Amenities details (type, attributes etc) are identified by specific letters. For additional details on the list of code sets used inside the amenity segments, please refer to the Technical Detail of the service.

### How to associate an Amenity to a given Cabin Class

Each amenity has a reference number given in the <amenityReference> section of the <amenityDetails>. Each travel solutions is given by all the information contained in the <> section. Inside this section, the cabin class details of each travel segment are given inside the <groupOfFares\> section. Amenity are referenced to the given cabin class inside the <referencingDetails> of the <fareFamiliesRef\> group. More specifically, anytime the letter "I" is returned in the <refQualifier\> field, the number contained in the <refNumber\> is associated to the number given in the <ameinityReference>. If several amenities are to be associated to the given Cabin Class, a repetition of the <referencingDetail\> is used. 

**Example :**

The following example shows the association between the Cabin Class M of the cabin W with the two Amenities 1 and 2.

...

<groupOfFares\>

<productInformation\> <= Group given the cabin class information

<cabinProduct\>

<rbd>M</rbd>

<cabin>W</cabin>

</productInformation\>

<fareFamiliesRef\>

<referencingDetail\>

<refQualifier\>**I**</refQualifier\>

<refNumber\>**1**</refNumber\>

</referencingDetail\>

<referencingDetail\>

<refQualifier\>**I**</refQualifier\>

<refNumber\>**2**</refNumber\>

</referencingDetail\>

</fareFamiliesRef\>

</groupOfFares\>

...

<amenitiesGroup>

<amentities>

<amenityDetails>

<amenityReference>**1**</amenityReference>

<amenityType>P</amenityType>

</amenityDetails>

<amenityDetails>

<amenityReference>**2**</amenityReference>

<amenityType>B</amenityType>

</amenityDetails>

</amentities>

</amenitiesGroup>

**Note :** In the XML returned in output, the Amenity group is always displayed after the Cabin Class information containing the reference to the AmenityReference.

### How to suppress retrieval of Amenities

Only a request level deactivation of amenities can be performed via the provisioning of the flag XAN (Deactivate Amenities) sent in the PTK segment. The input structure otherwise remains unchanged. 

EDIFACT Example: 

Deactivation for processing amenities can be achieved by: PTK+XAN’ 

WS Example:

<fareOptions>

<pricingTickInfo>

<pricingTicketing>

<priceType>XAN</priceType>

</pricingTicketing>

</pricingTickInfo>

</fareOptions>

## 5.113 Operation: 09.08 Output option - Reason of reject display

The Multiple Recommendation Pricer / Amadeus Live Check product can provide the reason of reject for the travel solutions which did not result in proposing valid recommendations. The recommendation is still proposed with propoer categorization of the failure reason and association of a monetary amount equal to 0.00. This is achieved via proper configuration settings performed on the OID

The failure to price can occur due to several reasons like either the travel solution not being available anymore or that there are no fares available for teh requested itinerary etc.

Following are the reject reasons that could be returned

**Reject code**

**Reject reason description**

NAV

When no availability is found for the travel solution and the posting is effectively 0 for all RBDs.

MCT

When Minimum Connection Time is not respected either due to schedule change / flight cancellation.

SCH

When the flight schedule is not available in the inventory anymore. Expected when the flight is cancelled.

TMO

This reject will encompass both the cases - global timeouts & accelerations

NFA

This will be returned only if we are not able to categorize the timeout during the fare exploration process or when we reached an end to fare exploration process but didn’t find any fares filed.

MIX

Applicable for Extended Air Choice (EAC) only. EAC doesn’t offer the possibility to mix travel solutions belonging to different distribution methods to create and propose a recommendation

UDM

Applicable for Extended Air Choice (EAC) only. Unidentified distribution method received in the input request.

When all proposed segments are rejected an additional error message NO VALID RECOMMENDATIONS FOUND has been put in place to relay information in first glance that the multiple recommendation pricer request has resulted in the evaluation of no valid recommendations; implying that all the travel solutions have some reason of reject attributed to them in the MRP response.

When all the reject reasons returned are TMO, the associated ERC (ErrorCode) is – 414.

When all reject reasons are != TMO or there is a mix of reject reasons with TMO returned in the response, the associated ERC – is 415.

## 5.114 Operation: 09.09 Output Option - Display ATPCO Fare Details

This option when activated (to note OID level activation required for benefiting from this feature) will lead to display of a few fare details sought by the customer namely cited below:

1.  ATPCO Fare Class
2.  ATPCO Tariff Number
3.  ATPCO Rule Number

Pre-requisites for the activation of this feature are as follows:

1.  OID level activation of the feature to display ATPCO fare details
2.  Display Change and Refund (Minirules) requested in the user's request

The output is received in the response at the location : /Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoardSearchReply/recommendation/paxFareProduct/fareDetails/groupOfFares/ticketInfos/additionalFareDetails

**Field Name**

**XML XPath**

**Example**

ATPCO Fare Class

/Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoardSearchReply/recommendation/paxFareProduct/fareDetails/groupOfFares/ticketInfos/additionalFareDetails/**rateClass**

KMLV2HO

ATPCO Tariff Number

/Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoardSearchReply/recommendation/paxFareProduct/fareDetails/groupOfFares/ticketInfos/additionalFareDetails/**pricingGroup**

21

ATPCO Rule Number

/Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoardSearchReply/recommendation/paxFareProduct/fareDetails/groupOfFares/ticketInfos/additionalFareDetails/**secondRateClass**

5901

Syntax for requesting Display Change and Refund (minirules) in the input:

<fareOptions\>  
  <pricingTickInfo\>  
    <pricingTicketing\>  
      **<priceType\>MNR</priceType\>**  
    </pricingTicketing\>  
  </pricingTickInfo\>  
</fareOptions\>

Syntax in the output to receive ATPCO fare details:

<recommendation>  
    <paxFareProduct>  
        <fareDetails>  
            <groupOfFares>  
                <ticketInfos>  
                    <additionalFareDetails>  
                        <rateClass>**KMLV2HO**</rateClass> <!-- ATPCO Fare Class -->  
                        <ticketDesignator>EOL4</ticketDesignator> <!-- Ticket Designator -->  
                        <pricingGroup>**21**</pricingGroup> <!-- ATPCO Tariff Number -->  
                        <secondRateClass>**5901**</secondRateClass> <!-- ATPCO Rule Number -->  
                    </additionalFareDetails>  
                </ticketInfos>  
            </groupOfFares>  
        </fareDetails>  
    </paxFareProduct>  
</recommendation>

To note : The fare details will be displayed only when the fare provider is ATPCO. The ticketDesignator may / may not be displayed in the output.

## 5.115 Operation: 09.10 Output Option - Sustainability : Display Carbon Footprint

Committed to the sustainability of future travel the option of displaying the Carbon Footprint of the journey will be displayed in the search response. To note that the emissions themselves will be retrieved from a third party provider which computes them; Amadeus will not be held responsible for the carbon emission values received. **Currently only these providers are assimilated - ICAO and Travalyst (TVYS).**

These carbon emissions will be retrieved based on the designated provider for each transportation mode - flight / train / bus. There would be a possibility to override the provider to be considered for each transportation mode to suit the requestor needs better. 

In addition, the computation methodology used for both reference and estimated carbon emissions can be overridden in input. Currently only possible if the provider is Travalyst and the transportation mode is flight. Two methodologies are handled:

\- Tank-to-Wake (TTW): Emissions produced by burning jet fuel during takeoff, flight, and landing of an aircraft.

\- Well-to-Wake (WTW): The sum of Well-to-Tank (WTT), emissions generated during the production, processing, handling, and delivery of jet fuel, and Tank-to-Wake (TTW) emissions.

**Request** \-

Since the provider of Carbon emissions may vary from one transportation mode to the other (when mixed content is activated for an office id) the user has a possibility to override and choose a provider of their preference. The request has to be provided in format specified below in order to override the default carbon emission providers of choice:

**Input option syntax** when single provider is chosen for multiple transportation modes:

     <carbonEmissionBySourceDetails>  
        <providerPerTransportation>  
                <carbonEmissionProviderCd>**ICAO**</carbonEmissionProviderCd>  
                <transportationModeType>**TRN**</transportationModeType>  
                <transportationModeType>**FLT**</transportationModeType>  
        </providerPerTransportation>  
    </carbonEmissionBySourceDetails>

Where ICAO is the provider code chosen by the requestor to retrieve the estimated carbon emissions for flights and trains

**Input option syntax** when each transportation mode has a different provider:

   <carbonEmissionBySourceDetails>  
        <providerPerTransportation>  
                <carbonEmissionProviderCd>**ICAO**</carbonEmissionProviderCd>  
                <transportationModeType>**TRN**</transportationModeType>  
        </providerPerTransportation>  
        <providerPerTransportation>  
                <carbonEmissionProviderCd>**TVYS**</carbonEmissionProviderCd>  
                <transportationModeType>**FLT**</transportationModeType>  
        </providerPerTransportation>  
    </carbonEmissionBySourceDetails>

**Input option syntax** when methodology WTW is speicifed:

   <carbonEmissionBySourceDetails>  
        <providerPerTransportation>  
                <carbonEmissionProviderCd>**TVYS**</carbonEmissionProviderCd>  
                <computationMethod>**WTW**</computationMethod>  
                <transportationModeType>**FLT**</transportationModeType>  
        </providerPerTransportation>  
    </carbonEmissionBySourceDetails>

**Response** \-

The information regarding the carbon emissions received in the response are as follows:

1. Carbon Emission Provider utilized for fetching the estimated carbon details per transportation mode.

**Syntax**:

   <carbonEmissionBySourceDetails>  
        <providerPerTransportation>  
                <carbonEmissionProviderCd>**ICAO**</carbonEmissionProviderCd>  
                <transportationModeType>**TRN**</transportationModeType>  
        </providerPerTransportation>  
        <providerPerTransportation>  
                <carbonEmissionProviderCd>**TVYS**</carbonEmissionProviderCd>  
                <computationMethod>**WTW**</computationMethod>  
                <transportationModeType>**FLT**</transportationModeType>  
        </providerPerTransportation>  
    </carbonEmissionBySourceDetails>

2. Reference Carbon emissions for a bound or proposed segment (Available only by targeting certain providers). 

**Syntax**:

   <referenceCarbonEmission>  
        <carbonEmissionByCabin>  
                <cabin>**M**</cabin>  
                <quantity>**834**</quantity>  
        </carbonEmissionByCabin>  
    </referenceCarbonEmission>

3. Estimated Carbon emissions for a flight or a segment. 

**Syntax**:

    <estimatedCarbonEmission>  
        <carbonEmissionByCabin>  
                <cabin>**M**</cabin>  
                <quantity>**478**</quantity>  
        </carbonEmissionByCabin>  
    </estimatedCarbonEmission>

## 5.120 Operation: 10.05 Ancillary Services option - pulled/pushed mode at sub-code level

This operation allows to specify for each service request if it should be processed in a pushed (informative mode) or pulled mode (service amount taken into account in the determination of the lowest recommendations).

The default mode is the pushed mode PUS. It can be specified or not.

In the following example, the two first requests for service AAA and BBB are in pulled mode.

Inclusion mode is the default mode. It can be specified or not.

Requests for CCC, DDD, EEE are all equivalent. PUS (default pushed mode) and IN (default inclusion mode) can be specified or not.

NOTE: the pulled mode option is not yet available.

## 5.121 Operation: 10.06 Ancillary Services option - Service coverage option

This option allows the process to match a service depending on its coverage applicability.

The service coverage option can be requested at:

-   Itinerary level (COI option). This is the default mode.
-   Flight level (COF option).
-   Bound level (COB option).
-   Itinerary level or a sub-coverage of the itinerary (CIS option).
-   Bound level or a sub-coverage of the bound (CIB option).

Each service request can be associated with a specific coverage option as shown below.

## 5.126 Operation: 10.11 Ancillary Services option - Seat characteristic request

This option allows to request a specific service: seat characteristics in service group SA.

Only one seat characteristic by input request will be processed:

-   All sequences filed with more than one seat characteristic, can't be matched.
-   If several seat characteristics are present in one input request, all but the first one will be ignored.

Only one seat characteristic is displayed in the output: for a request where no seat characteristic is specified the last seat characteristic matched will be the one displayed even if there are different seat characteristic on the segments of the journey.

This display is independent of the price associated to the seat characteristic and the sequence order in the filing.

## 5.127 Operation: 10.12 Ancillary Services option - Multi Passengers request

In case of a multi passenger request, it is important to note that the monetary information  will be returned by passenger type and not by passenger.

## 5.129 Operation: 11.1 Smart Switch option - Force live traffic

This option enables you to force a call to Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoard service without going through a Fare\_InstantMasterPricertransaction.

The activation is done with the "FLT" - Force Live Trafic parameter set in the <priceType>field oft he <pricingTickInfo> (PTK Segment), see example below.

<fareOptions>

    <pricingTickInfo>

          <pricingTicketing>

                <priceType>FLT</priceType>

          </pricingTicketing>

       </pricingTickInfo>

</fareOptions>

## 5.130 Operation: 11.2 Smart Switch option - No live traffic

This option enables you to force a call only to the Fare\_InstantTravelBoardSearch transaction. No calls to Fare\_MasterPricerTravelBoard transaction are performed and only Instant Search content is retrieved.

The activation is done with the "NLT" - No Live Trafic parameter set in the <priceType>field oft he <pricingTickInfo> (PTK Segment), see example below.

<fareOptions>

    <pricingTickInfo>

          <pricingTicketing>

                <priceType>NLT</priceType>

          </pricingTicketing>

       </pricingTickInfo>

</fareOptions>

In this case, the response contains the "IMP" code retrieved in the <advisoryTypeInfo> field of the <replyStatus> (STX) segment as shown in the example below. 

  <replyStatus>

      <status>

            <advisoryTypeInfo>IMP</advisoryTypeInfo>

      </status>

</replyStatus>

In case no content is contained, an error message "DATA DOMAIN UPDATE ON-GOING" is returned. This message means new data is being added into the Instant Search Cache. In case you receive such error message, we invite you to wait a couple of minute before sending back the query, so that the upload of data is completed in the Instant Search cache.

## 5.131 Operation: 12.1 Shopping Travel Platform option - add external NDC content

Recommendations received through NDC chanel are merged with classic GDS recommendations.  
Those recommendations will be flagged (N) in the Master Pricer response messsage to be recognised among all all of them .  
In addition, the Owner of all offers included in the group of recommendations is setup at the company level.  
<recommendation>  
<itemNumber\>  
            <itemNumberId>  
                <number>1</number>  
            </itemNumberId>  
            <codeShareDetails\>  
                <company>LGH</company>      : Owner  
            </codeShareDetails\>  
            <priceTicketing\>  
                <priceType\>N</priceType\>      : recommendation coming from NDC  
            </priceTicketing\>  
        </itemNumber\>  
....  
< ecommendation>

  
In order to price the correct NDC recommendation, a list of mandatory information must be provided :   
\-         The ResponseID :

The Response ID is the same for all its associated offers.

\-         The OfferID :

The list of OfferID in the final MP response is only fed with NDC content. This means no GDS offers are generated .  
This list is ordered by price and each offer with the same price is alphanumerically sorted.

\-         The OfferItemID :

In a same Offer, the list of OfferItem returned is alphanumerically sorted.  
From the NDC content, in the Airshopping reply, each OfferItem is associated to a PTC. This means every passengers which have the same PTC are associated to this OfferItem.  
In order to keep this association in the MP reply and allow you to know which PTC is linked to which OfferItem, a reference is added for each OfferItem.  
  
  
<offersGroup>  
        <response>  
            <applicationDetails\>  
                <internalId\>XAamadeus5A96B7NN7</internalId\>   : responseID  
            </applicationDetails\>  
        </response>  
        <offers>  
            <offerDtetails>  
                <reference>1</reference>  
                <offerId>XAmadeus11</offerId>    : OfferID  
            </offerDtetails>  
            <offerItems>  
                <offerItemDetails>  
                    <offerItemId>XAmadeus11-1</offerItemId>   : OfferItemID  
                </offerItemDetails>  
            </offerItems>  
        </offers>  
    </offersGroup>

## 5.135 Operation: 12.5 Shopping Travel Platform option - NDC Traveller Profile (NOT FOR GDS CONTENT)

You have the possibility to input loyalty programs (Frequent Flyer, AF Subscriber card, QF relevant offers) for NDC airlines, in the MP query.

This input will be considered **ONLY FOR NDC CONTENT** and those parameters will be ignored by all the non-NDC processes.

The traveller profile contains loyalty programs associated to the passengers to which they belong (if any) and shall be input in the ndcQueryParameters group, starting with an OFD segment.

OFD+NDC'

<ndcMarker><reference>NDC</reference></ndcMarker>

## 5.136 Operation: 13.1 Bundles of services Option - Public Fare

This option allows travel agents to display sets of recommendations (less to the most restrictive ones), using fare conditions and services criteria in a comparable and standardised way in order for the traveller to be able to compare easily different offers from several providers and to ease upselling.

The Travel Agent specifies bundles in the query with the following information:

-   A name
-   A ranking to define upselling order
-   A set of criteria

The ranking of bundles determines the order of importance of the bundles and consequently the order of filling (3 numeric).

The bundles are filled by increasing ranking with recommendation ordered by price. As long as a recommendation matches a bundle, no recommendation is returned for bundle with a lower ranking.

For each flight initially returned by Master Pricer, the bundles allow to target a set of fares sharing the same characteristics defined by one or several criteria as listed below:

-   Baggage services
-   Fare conditions:
    -   Refundability
    -   Penalty
    -   Rebookability
-   Flight and fare criteria

## 5.136.3 Possible Errors

If too many Bundles are requested the whole query is rejected with the message: “TOO MANY REQUESTED BUNDLES” If, for any element of the bundle, too many occurrences are requested the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE - TOO MANY OCCURENCES REQUESTED” If a mandatory element of the bundle is not specified, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE – MANDATORY ELEMENT NOT SPECIFIED” If a same bundle name is used for more than one bundle, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE– INVALID NAME” If a same bundle ranking is used for more than one bundle, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE– INVALID RANKING” If the specified criteria are different than the ones existing, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE – INVALID CRITERIA TYPE” If the specified criteria are different than the ones associated to the bundle type, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE – INVALID CRITERIA(S)” If the specified Application is different than the ones associated to the bundle criteria, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE – INVALID APPLICATION”

* * *

## 5.137 Operation: 13.2 Bundles of services Option - Unifare

This option allows travel agents to display sets of recommendations (less to the most restrictive ones), using fare conditions and services criteria in a comparable and standardised way in order for the traveller to be able to compare easily different offers from several providers and to ease upselling. Please consult the "16.2 Bundes of Services - Public Fare" section for more information on Bundle activation and usage. 

The example below illustrates a search with two bundles targeting Unifare :

Name

Bundle

Ranking

LIGHT

At least 1 free baggage allowance

1

FULL

At least 1 free baggage allowance

\+ Refundable + Rebooking

2

**Remark** : Public Fares are triggered by adding the RU in the <value> field inside the <attribute> group of the <bucketDetail> segment.

## 5.138.3 Possible Errors

If too many Bundles are requested the whole query is rejected with the message: “TOO MANY REQUESTED BUNDLES” If, for any element of the bundle, too many occurrences are requested the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE - TOO MANY OCCURENCES REQUESTED” If a mandatory element of the bundle is not specified, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE – MANDATORY ELEMENT NOT SPECIFIED” If a same bundle name is used for more than one bundle, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE– INVALID NAME” If a same bundle ranking is used for more than one bundle, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE– INVALID RANKING” If the specified criteria are different than the ones existing, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE – INVALID CRITERIA TYPE” If the specified criteria are different than the ones associated to the bundle type, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE – INVALID CRITERIA(S)” If the specified Application is different than the ones associated to the bundle criteria, the whole query is rejected with the following message: “BUNDLE – INVALID APPLICATION”

## 5.140 Operation: 13.5 Bundles of services Option - MRP option in Bundle

Bundles option enables you to widen and customize the shopping search requesting for more recommendations and grouping them by same set of criteria. It allows to provide more relevant offers to the traveler to ease the upselling.

A bundle can be defined as a group of recommendations that share the same criteria that you defined. The types of criteria are ancillary services, free baggage allowance, refundability and changeability and some fare conditions like publishing carrier/ or type of fares. Please refer to the dedicated “Bundles of services” for further information.

For each standard recommendation, an alternative recommendation (if any bundle matches the criteria) is returned, maximum of 1 alternative recommendation per matching Bundle.

**ACTIVATION**

To use bundle, you must have the office ID enable for the use of the option.

The bundle option with MRP is activated in query with the “MRP” code set in <priceType\> of the < pricingTickInfo\> field.

For each bundle, each criteria is defined in different <bucketDetails> values contained in <BucketInfo> field. Please note that it is possible to insert up to 6 <BucketInfo> per query.

Example for several bundle for Booking Class upsell :

<buckets> <= First Bundle

<bucketInfo>

<name>ECO</name>

<mode>UPS</mode>

<weight>1</weight>

</bucketInfo>

</buckets>

…

<buckets> <= Maximum Sixth Bundle

<bucketInfo>

<name>FLEX</name>

<mode>UPS</mode>

<weight>6</weight>

</bucketInfo>

</buckets>

In Output, alternative recommendations are tagged with a “P” code set in the <refQualifier\> of the < segmentFlightRef\> field.

Example displaying one recommendation (number 1) belonging to Bundle 1 (BL) and having an alternative recommendation (P) displayed in recommendation (number 2):

<recommendation> <= First recommendation

<itemNumber\>

<itemNumberId>

<number>1</number>

</itemNumberId>

</itemNumber\>

…

< segmentFlightRef\>

<referencingDetail\>

<refQualifier\>BL</refQualifier\> <= Recommendation matches Bundle 1

<refNumber\>1</referenceNumber\>

<refQualifier\>P</refQualifier\> <= Alternative recommendation existing in ItemNumber 2

<refNumber\>2</referenceNumber\>

</referencingDetail\>

< /segmentFlightRef\>

</recommendation>

<recommendation> <= alternative recommendation

<itemNumber\>

<itemNumberId>

<number>2</number>

</itemNumberId>

</itemNumber\>

…

< segmentFlightRef\>

<referencingDetail\>

<refQualifier\>BL</refQualifier\> <= Alternative Recommendation matches Bundle 2

<refNumber\>2</referenceNumber\>

</referencingDetail\>

< /segmentFlightRef\>

</recommendation>

**COMPATIBILITY AND LIMITATIONS**

Bundles option can be used for any type of itineraries with maximum 2 requested segments (Round-trip, One-way, Open Jaw).

A query can contain up to 6 bundles.

Bundle option is not combinable with:

-   Upsell
-   Buckets
-   Standard Multi-ticket
-   Alternate Price

## 5.141 Operation: 13.6 Bundles of services Option - Force Ascending Logic for Bundle processing

This input option forces the bundles to be computed and sets of recommendations proposed in a strictly increasing order of price.

Example: Assuming if a travel solution matches and leads to valid recommendations proposed for all the bundles defined in the input criteria (based on ranking); **they would necessarily be in ascending order of price**. Cheapest < Recommendation satisfying bundle#1 < bundles#2 < bundle#3 (assuming bundle ranks are ascending in order too)

Syntax (input): 

<fareOptions\>  
  <pricingTickInfo\>  
    <pricingTicketing\>  
      **<priceType\>ALB</priceType\>**  
    </pricingTicketing\>  
  </pricingTickInfo\>  
</fareOptions\>

This option has no affectation on the output, it affects only the processing logic.

## 5.142 Operation: 14.1 Baggage Option - Free Baggage Allowance

This feature of Master Pricer provides the information about the free baggage allowed for each recommendation.

The functionality is triggered by a setting at OID level or by input option (FBA) with 2 values:

-   1: allows to return FBA
-   0: no FBA is returned

The input option overrides the OID setting.

In the example below, the Free Baggage Allowance is requested by input option.

In the reply, we have 2 recommendations with different baggage allowances:

-   Request segment 1: BCN-MAD
-   Request segment 2: MAD-VLC

The free baggage allowance is returned with the following information:

Free baggage allowed

Applicability

First recommendation with same FBA for the whole itinerary

BCN-MAD 23 Kg

MAD-IBZ-VLC 23 Kg

23 kg on Requested segment 1 – Leg 1

23 kg on Requested segment 2 – Leg 1 and 2

Second recommendation with different  FBA

BCN-MAD 1PC

MAD- VLC    2 PC

1P on Requested segment 1 – Leg 1

2P on Requested segment 2 – Leg 1

Baggage allowance is detailed at 3 levels:

-   Free Baggage Allowance information (number of pieces or number of kilos)
-   Baggage allowance coverage (Passenger type reference, flight coverage, baggage allowance reference)
-   Baggage allowance coverage reference at recommendation level

Free Baggage Allowance is detailed in freeBagAllowanceGrp:

FBA #1

23 Kilos

FBA #2

1 Piece

FBA #3

2 Pieces

1

Requested segment 2 – Leg 1 and 2

1

## 5.143 Operation: 14.2 Baggage Option - Free Baggage Allowance with multiple passenger types

In case of different passenger types are requested in the query of Master Pricer, the free baggage allowance always provide the information of the ADT passenger type if present in the query. If no ADT passenger type is requested, the free baggage allowance is provided for the first passenger type.

In this example, we consider 2 PTCs:  1 ADT and 1 CH and one recommendation:

-   Request segment 1: BCN-MAD
-   Request segment 2: MAD-VLC

Passenger Type

Free baggage allowed

Applicability

Recommendation with multiple  passenger types

ADT

CH

BCN-MAD  1P

MAD-IBZ-VLC 1P

1 piece on Requested segment 1 – Leg 1 and 1 pice on Requested segment 2 – Leg 1 and 2

Baggage allowance is detailed at 3 levels:

-   Free Baggage Allowance information (number of pieces or number of kilos)
-   Baggage allowance coverage (Passenger type references, flight coverage, baggage allowance reference )
-   Baggage allowance coverage reference at recommendation level

Baggage Allowance is detailed in freeBagAllowanceGrp:

FBA #1

1 piece

Baggage coverage is detailed in serviceCoverageInfoGrp:

Passenger type reference

Flight coverage

Reference to FBA

Baggage coverage #1

1 (ADT)

Requested segment 1 – Leg 1

Requested segment 2 – Leg 1 and 2

FBA #1

Recommendation details:

Reference to Baggage coverage

Recommendation  #1

Baggage coverage #1

## 5.144 Operation: 14.3 Baggage Option - Detailed Free Baggage allowance

The functionality allows to return the detailed FBA when the FBA is described in piece concept with the number of pieces greater than 0.

The detailed FBA is returned only for authorized baggage (number greater than 0).

Only the first 4 filed baggage are returned.

Commercial names are returned as free text.

Only for Adult PTC or for the 1st PTC like FBA.

The functionality is activated by input option (FBD).

The example bellow illustrates the following:

Reco #

Free Baggage Allowance

Free Baggage Allowance Details

Number and subcode

Commercial name

1

1 piece

//01/0GO

UPTO50LB 23KG AND62LI 158LCM

2

1 piece

//01/0GO

UPTO50LB 23KG BAGGAGE

//01/0DD

SKI EQUIPMENT UP TO 50LB 23KG

## 5.145 Operation: 14.4 Baggage Option - Baggage Option (1)

With the baggage option, the information about cheapest baggage for each recommendation returned by MasterPricer depends on data provided by related airline systems. At the moment only Full Service Carriers are sharing this information with Amadeus. Those baggage could be free (from free baggage allowance filling and returned in FBA fields) or at charge (from AAS filling and returned in AAS fields).

AAS baggage are processed from ATPCO source, from service classification P/C/F as in the catalogue/pricing process (only if the Airline has signed an agreement with Amadeus for Ancillary Services distribution).

-   **Service classification P**: Prepaid baggage that can be purchased prior to passenger airport check-in
-   **Service classification C**: Baggage charges that apply at airport check-in
-   **Service classification F:** Other type of baggage

If the airline do not file baggage in piece concept, the number of KG allowed is returned plus the price for one additional KG.

**Recommendation 1**

**Recommendation 2**

**Recommendation 3**

**Recommendation 4**

Airline in piece concept

Airline in piece concept

Airline in piece concept

Airline in weight concept

FBA = 0

FBA = 1

FBA = 2

FBA >= 0

AAS bag occurrence 1 & 2 returned**\***

AAS bag occurrence 1 returned

No AAS bag returned

Pricer per KG returned

FBA & AAS type P/C processed in Master Pricer are **compliant with IATA resolution 302 & USDOT** that regulate the calculation of baggage (quantity and fees).

\* Important: only 1 occurrence of AAS baggage is displayed until the activation of occurrence process in catalogue in order to ensure the consistency between shopping & catalogue.

**Passenger Type Code process:** The AAS is only calculated for the adult passenger type (if any).

For example, if we have an adult, a child and an infant, the AAS returned is the one applicable to the adult.

In case no adult passenger type is requested, the AAS returned is the one of the first passenger type of the query.

Free Baggage information will be automatically processed when baggage option is requested (even if FBA is not activated). C.f. Free Baggage Allowance.

Each recommendation could be cut into several BTU (portion of travel on which one given carrier defines the unique applicable Baggage allowance and charges policy). In that case, FBA and AAS information will be returned per BTU. The price of the baggage for the entire itinerary can be calculated by adding the price of the baggage on each BTU.

Example of baggage information returned on a recommendation:

**BTU 1**

**BTU 2**

**BTU 3**

FBA = 0

FBA = 1

FBA = 1

AAS bag occurrence 1 is 10 euros & occurrence 2 is 12 euros

AAS bag occurrence 1 is 5 euros

AAS bag occurrence 1 is 7 euros

The price for the first baggage on the entire itinerary is 10 euros (one baggage already included on BTU 2 & 3).

The price for a second baggage is:   12 + 5 + 7 = 24 euros.

After the flight booking and pricing, it is recommended to send an AAS catalogue/pricing query to retrieve and book/price Ancillary Services. This catalogue query should be limited to the portions of the itinerary where the at-charge baggage is necessary.

Example of itinerary Paris-London-Mexico:

**Paris - London**

**London – Mexico**

Airline in piece concept

Airline in piece concept

FBA = 0

FBA = 1

AAS bag occurrence 1 & 2 returned

AAS bag occurrence 1 returned

If the end user wants to travel with one baggage, an AAS baggage has to be bought on Paris-London part only (as a baggage is already included on the fare for London-Mexico).

Baggage activation

This option is triggered by a setting at OID level and by the input option BAG in Master Picer query:

     <fareOptions\>

        <pricingTickInfo\>

            <pricingTicketing\>

                <priceType\>**BAG**</priceType\>

            </pricingTicketing\>

        </pricingTickInfo\>

    </fareOptions\>

Baggage information returned in the output

For each AAS baggage, the following information is returned (if filled):

Price / RFIC / RFISC / SSR code / Booking Method / Service classification (P, C or F) / Commercial Name / Carrier / Group / Subgroup / Description 1 & 2

-   **RFIC/RFISC:** Reason For Issuance Code/ Reason For Issuance Sub Code
-   **SSR code:** Special Service Request

The service classification P correspond to prepaid baggage, which mean that the returned AAS price is only available until a certain time before the check-in. An AAS will be returned in type P only if the conditions are still applicable. In service classification C, the baggage price will be the same at check-in time.

## 5.147 Operation: 14.6 Baggage Option - AAS Bagage Media ID

The AAS baggage media ID allows to have a visual representation of the service. It is returned if it has been filed in ATPCo.

The reply illustrates a service with media ID:

-   Sub code: 0CC
-   Group: BG
-   Description 1: B1
-   Media ID: 10824949
-   Airline: 6X
-   Commercial name: FIRST CHECKED BAG UPTO 23KG

## 5.148 Operation: 14.7 Baggage Option - Free Carry-on Baggage Allowance

This feature of Master Pricer provides the information about the free carry-on baggage allowed (COA) for each recommendation.

The functionality is triggered by a setting at OID level or by input option (COA) with 2 values:

-   1: allows to return COA
-   0: no COA is returned

The input option overrides the OID setting.

**Input option syntax** when specified at request level:

     <fareOptions\>  
        <feeIdDescription>  
            <feeId\>  
                <feeType\>**COA**</feeType\>  
                <feeIdNumber\>**1**</feeIdNumber\>  
            </feeId\>  
        </feeIdDescription>  
    </fareOptions\>

In the example below, the Free Carry-on Baggage Allowance is requested by input option.

In the reply, we have 2 recommendations with different baggage allowances:

-   Request segment 1: BCN-MAD
-   Request segment 2: MAD-VLC

The free carry-on baggage allowance is returned with the following information:

Free carry-on baggage allowed

Applicability

First recommendation with same COA for the whole itinerary

BCN-MAD 23 Kg

MAD-IBZ-VLC 23 Kg

23 kg on Requested segment 1 – Leg 1

23 kg on Requested segment 2 – Leg 1 and 2

Second recommendation with different  COA

BCN-MAD 1PC

MAD- VLC    2 PC

1P on Requested segment 1 – Leg 1

2P on Requested segment 2 – Leg 1

Baggage allowance is detailed at 3 levels:

-   Free Carry-on Baggage Allowance information (number of pieces or number of kilos)
-   Baggage allowance coverage (Passenger type reference, flight coverage, baggage allowance reference)
-   Baggage allowance coverage reference at recommendation level

Free Baggage Allowance is detailed in freeBagAllowanceGrp:

FBA #1

23 Kilos

FBA #2

1 Piece

FBA #3

2 Pieces

Baggage coverage is detailed in serviceCoverageInfoGrp:

Passenger type reference

Flight coverage

Reference to FBA

Baggage coverage #1

1

Requested segment 1 – Leg 1

Requested segment 2 – Leg 1 and 2

COA #1

Baggage  coverage #2

1

Requested segment 1 – Leg 1

Requested segment 2 – Leg 1

COA #2

COA #3

Recommendation details:

Reference to Baggage coverage

Recommendation  #1

Baggage coverage #1

Recommendation #2

Baggage coverage #2

**Syntax output**:  
     <serviceFeesGrp>  
       <serviceTypeInfo>  
         <carrierFeeDetails\>  
           <type>FBA</type>  
         </carrierFeeDetails\>  
       </serviceTypeInfo>  
       <serviceCoverageInfoGrp>  
         <itemNumberInfo>  
           <itemNumber\>  
             <number>1</number>  
             **<qualifier>COA</qualifier>  <!-- The qualifier when not filled with any value or not present implies FBA and value as COA is present it impies that the service coverage/ association with passengers etc is for the free carry-on baggage allowance -->**  
           </itemNumber\>  
         </itemNumberInfo>

There is otherwise no change in the way baggage details are defined / coverage / passenger level association is defined. The output interpretation similar to FBA applies.

## 5.149 Operation: 16.1 Relevance and Data Driven Search

Master Pricer can return a distribution of the recommendations through different "buckets". A bucket gathers recommendations with common criteria beyond the price dimension (carrier, direct flights, flight convenience and so on).

**Bucket**

**Description**

**Examples**

Standard (STD)

Returns the cheapest recommendations.

<bucketDetails>

<code>STD</code>

</bucketDetails>

Online Carrier (ONL)

Returns the recommendations with the requested online carriers for the itinerary. The online carrier is the marketing carrier of the itinerary.

Online carriers can be include (INC, default) or exclude (EXC). If no carrier code is specified as attribute, the existing online carriers for the requested itinerary is equally distributed. In this case, no application is defined.

<bucketDetails>

<code>ONL</code>

<attribute>

<value>LH</value>

<value>AF</value>

</attribute>

</bucketDetails>

Main Carrier (MCX)

Returns the recommendations with the requested main carriers per segment or for the whole itinerary. The main carrier is the marketing carrier with the longest flying time of the itinerary or segment.

Main carriers can be include (INC, default) or exclude (EXC).

If no carrier code is specified, the existing main carriers for the requested itinerary or segments (if segments number are specified) is equally distributed. In this case, no application is defined.

<bucketDetails>

<code>MCX</code>

<type>INC</type>

<attribute>

<value>LH</value>

<value>AF</value>

</attribute>

</bucketDetails>

Time Window (TIW)

Returns the recommendations matching the requested time window of departure or arrival per segment.

The time granularity is the hour. Attributes have to be specified for at least one requested segment.

D/A to indicate departure or arrival + Time (24H format) + Time window (+/- y hours with y in the range \[1-12\])

<bucketDetails>

<code>TIW</code>

<attribute>

<requestedSgt>1</requestedSgt>

<value>D</value>

<value>0800</value>

<value>2</value>

</attribute>

<attribute>

<requestedSgt>2</requestedSgt>

<value>A</value>

<value>2100</value>

<value>1</value>

</attribute>

</bucketDetails>

Time of Departure (TIM)

Returns the recommendations matching the requested period of departure per segment.

If no attribute is specified, the recommendations are equally distributed on the different periods of departure.

AM (Morning 6H-11H59)

PM (Afternoon 12H-7H59)

EV (Evening 18H-23H59)

NI (Night 00H-5H59)

<bucketDetails>

<code>TIM</code>

<attribute>

<requestedSgt>1</requestedSgt>

<value>AM</value>

</attribute>

<attribute>

<requestedSgt>2</requestedSgt>

<value>EV</value>

<value>NI</value>

</attribute>

</bucketDetails>

Number of Connecting Flights (CFL)

Returns the recommendations with the requested maximum number of connecting flights for the itinerary.

One attribute must be specified and attribute count cannot be used.

NSP (Direct non-stop)

DIR (Direct)

1CX (1 connection maximum)

2CX (2 connections maximum)

3CX (3 connections maximum)

<bucketDetails>

<code>CFL</code>

<attribute>

<value>NSP</value>

</attribute>

</bucketDetails>

Type of Fare (TPF)

Returns the recommendations with the requested type of fares for the itinerary. Some type of fares cannot be requested at the same time as attributes. RU and RW type of fares cannot be combined with RB, RA, RC, RN, RZ, RD, RX and RV.

If no type of fare is specified as attribute, a distribution will be done on type of fares RP, RU and RW for the requested itinerary.

For RW type of fare, corporate codes or names have to be specified in the input query.

<bucketDetails>

<code>TPF</code>

<attribute>

<value>RU</value>

<value>RW</value>

</attribute>

</bucketDetails>

No Advance Purchase (NAP)

Returns the recommendations matching no advance purchase restrictions for the itinerary.

<bucketDetails>

<code>NAP</code>

</bucketDetails>

No Penalty (NPE)

Returns the recommendations matching no penalty restriction for the itinerary.

<bucketDetails>

<code>NPE</code>

</bucketDetails>

No Time Restrictions (NDA)

Returns the recommendations matching no time restrictions for the itinerary.

<bucketDetails>

<code>NDA</code>

</bucketDetails>

Refundable (RFA)

Returns the recommendations matching refundable restriction for the itinerary.

<bucketDetails>

<code>RFA</code>

</bucketDetails>

Non Refundable (NRF)

Returns the recommendations matching non-refundability restriction for the itinerary.

<bucketDetails>

<code>NRF</code>

</bucketDetails>

No Restrictions (NRS)

Returns the recommendations matching no restrictions for the itinerary.

<bucketDetails>

<code>NRS</code>

</bucketDetails>

Publishing Carrier (PBC)

Returns the recommendations with the requested online publishing carriers for the itinerary. Publishing carriers can be include (INC, default) or exclude (EXC).

If no carrier code is specified, the existing online publishing carriers for the requested itinerary is equally distributed. In this case, no application is defined.

<bucketDetails>

<code>PBC</code>

<type>EXC</type>

<attribute>

<value>CA</value>

</attribute>

</bucketDetails>

The example below illustrates a search with 5 buckets:

Cheapest

Standard (STD)

40 % of recommendations with lowest prices, whatever the travel convenience.

PreferredCarriers

Main Carrier (MCX)

10 % of recommendations with LH and AF main carriers.

OnlineDirect

Online Carrier (ONL)

Connecting Flights (CFL)

30 % of recommendations with online carriers and direct and non stop flights.

NoTimeRestrictions

No Time Restrictions (NDA)

15 % of recommendations with no time restrictions.

DepartureTime

Time of departure (TIM)

5 % of recommendations leaving on morning (AM) and returning on afternoon (AF), evening (EV) and night (NI).

## 5.150 Operation: 17.1 Display Change and Refund (Minirules)

You can request a summary of the most important elements of rules related to change and refund situations at recommendation level. The functionality is authorized by appropriate settings at OID level and triggered by input option (MNR).

**Input syntax -**

   <fareOptions>  
        <pricingTickInfo>  
            <pricingTicketing>  
                **<priceType>MNR</priceType>**  
            </pricingTicketing>  
        </pricingTickInfo>  
    </fareOptions>

The following information is returned for each recommendation:

-   Conditions for change with revalidation and the maximum applicable revalidation penalty fee per journey
-   Conditions for change with reissue and the minimum and maximum applicable reissue penalty fees per journey
-   Refund conditions and the minimum and maximum applicable refund penalty fees per journey with time bounds
-   Category 16 matched and contains free-form text

Only before departure related data are returned.

The currency applicable to the penalty amounts is the same currency as the currency applicable to the recommendations.

The currency of the penalty amounts may therefore reflect input options such as currency conversion or selling city override options.

When multiple passengers, penalty amounts are computed for 1 passenger only.

Keyword

Description

Value

ASS

The category is not coded, not validated or negated

None

FFT

Part of rule is free form text from category 16

1 if part of the rule is free form text from category 16

RVJ

Revalidation of ticket before departure

0 if not allowed  
1 if allowed with restrictions

BDJ

Reissue/Refund of ticket before departure

0 if not allowed  
1 if allowed with restrictions

BDC

Revalidation maximum penalty amount for the ticket

Amount (default value: 0)

BDT

Reissue/Refund maximum penalty amount for the ticket

Amount (default value: 0)

BDS

Reissue/Refund minimum penalty amount for the ticket (specific actvation required )

Amount (default value: 0)

BDP

Refund time-based penalty amount for the ticket (specific actvation required)

Amount (default value: 0)

30.00 euros (BDS)

Assumption (ASS)

Refund allowed (BDJ)

300.00 euros (BDT)

300 euros 72h before departure (BDP)

100.00 euros (BDS)

100 euros 24h before departure (BDP)

Refund not allowed (BDJ)

## 5.150.3 Possible Errors

If display change / refund conditions or minirules option is requested in input but not authorized via configuration "Invalid option" error message is raised.

* * *

## 5.151 Operation: 17.2 Reliability flag for Display Change and Refund (minirules)

The guarantee tag is optional on the STX output message. It gives an information of reliability of the Change and Refund conditions (mini rules). If Cat 31 and/or Cat 33 are not filed, the Display Change and Refund (Mini Rules) process will automatically check the content of Cat 16. In this case, the guarantee value of the tag will be ‘0’.

Otherwise, the guarantee tag has the value ‘1’.

## 5.152 Operation: 18.1 Display miles accrual

The functionality is activated via input option (DMA).

## 5.154 Operation: 20.1 Optional Data Profile

The user has the ability to request some specific data profiles at query level via input option.

When optional data profiles are specified in input, they override the standard data profile.

Up to twenty optional data profiles can be requested simultaneously.

The query bellow describes a search with "OPT MPLITE" Optional Data Profile specified.

The activation of the Optional Data Profile is performed by inserted the "OPTDP" option in the <FeeType> of the <FeeIdDescription> group of the input of Master Pricer. 

<feeIdDescription>

<feeId>

<feeType> **OPTDP** </feeType>

</feeId>

</feeIdDescription>

## 5.154.3 Possible Errors

If the optional data profile requested is not attached to the office ID, the query is rejected with the following error message:

"OPTIONAL DATA PROFILE NOT AUTHORISED"

If two optional data profiles overriding the same FS Parameters are requested, the query is rejected with the following error message:

"CONFLICTING DATA PROFILES REQUESTED"

* * *

## 5.155 Operation: 21.1 A/B Testing

The A/B testing is a setting for clients that allows to redirect a portion of shopping transactions from that client to different internal configurations. Part of the flow which is not redirected is called flow A, and the one redirected is denoted flow B. This allows comparing efficiency of triggering special settings for some customers, notably in terms of conversion, i.e. the look to book ratio.

In some case, Amadeus randomly drives the AB Testing flow. 

If not, the AB test flow can be activated using one of the following qualifier depending on the underlying configuration :

\- ABT in PTK Segment.

\- ABR in ATR Segment.

The Flow can be disactivated using the NAB qualifier in the PTK Segment.

## 5.156 Operation: 22.1 Low Cost Carriers in MPT

The user has the possibility to have included in the reply, Low-Cost Content Carriers recommendations or mixed of Low-Cost Content Carriers and Full Service Carriers recommendations. The example below describes 3 recommendations. The first recommendation is a Ticketless Access Carrier recommendation (priceType **L**), the second one is a LCC Connect recommendation (priceType **Q**) and the third one is a Full Service Carriers recommendation.

-     **LCC Connect.**

This solution  abbreviated as 'LCC Connect' which would be restricted only for the Low cost carriers shopping flow and will require to use REST/JSON services after the search step performed thanks to Master Pricer.

New product code"Q"  introduced in the Shopping Response.

LCC are not activated by default on 1A side, Please contact your AM for activation.

Product Code Q will be present in the shopping response for Relevant recommendation under the PriceType Tag as shown below. Recommendation can include GDS,LCC Connect and Light Ticketing flow.

-   **Input Syntax**

No Specific change in the Input request, it will be same as usual MP flow.

-   **Output Syntax (**Ticketless Access Carrier: Pricetype L**)**

<recommendation>

        <itemNumber\>

            <itemNumberId>

                <number>11</number>

            </itemNumberId>

            <priceTicketing\>

                **<priceType\>L</priceType\>**

            </priceTicketing\>

        </itemNumber\>

        <recPriceInfo\>

            <monetaryDetail\>

                <amountType\>R</amountType\>

                <amount>157.49</amount>

            </monetaryDetail\>

        </recPriceInfo\>               

-   **Output Syntax (**LCC Connect: Pricetype: Q**)**  

<recommendation>

        <itemNumber\>

            <itemNumberId>

                <number>1</number>

            </itemNumberId>

            <priceTicketing\>

                **<priceType\>Q</priceType\>**

            </priceTicketing\>

        </itemNumber\>

        <recPriceInfo\>

            <monetaryDetail\>

                <amountType\>R</amountType\>

                <amount>0.00</amount>

            </monetaryDetail\>

        </recPriceInfo\>

-   **Output Syntax (**Full Service Carriers**)**

    <recommendation>

        <itemNumber\>

            <itemNumberId>

                <number>4</number>

            </itemNumberId>

        </itemNumber\>

        <recPriceInfo\>

            <monetaryDetail\>

                <amount>134.30</amount>

            </monetaryDetail\>

            <monetaryDetail\>

                <amount>36.30</amount>

            </monetaryDetail\>

        </recPriceInfo\>
